# workspace-knowledge

The workspace's Logseq knowledge graph: thread pages, journal captures, retrieval and the knowledge tools.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-workspace-knowledge.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-workspace-knowledge.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [logseq](logseq.md), [session](session.md), [tools](tools.md)
- **Required by:** [workspace](workspace.md)

## About

The workspace's knowledge lives in a Logseq graph (harness-logseq.el),
not in the harness's memory store.  A thread is a page, the durable
things the agent learns are blocks on it, and the conversation's
turns are captured in the day's journal under a link to the thread's
page.  The graph is the source of truth: the user can open it in
Logseq, edit or delete a block, and the next search reads what they
wrote.  Nothing here writes a second store or a cache.

The graph is the user's, not the harness's.  A workspace has a
`:graph` directory (defaulting to `harness-logseq-directory`, which
reads `LOGSEQ_HOME`), and several workspaces may share one graph:
every block says which workspace wrote it, so a search sees its own
workspace's knowledge unless it asks for the whole graph.

What is written when:

- `knowledge/thread-page`: the thread's page (`Threads/<title>`) with
  its identity block -- workspace, workspace id, thread id, status,
  project -- created when the thread starts and looked up by id;
- the capture: one journal block per message, with the thread's page
  as a link and the session and node as provenance;
- `knowledge/write`: a durable block on the thread's page, or on a
  page the agent names (`Projects/harness`, `Preferences`), which is
  what the knowledge tools write;
- `knowledge/thread-touch`: the thread page's status and last-touched
  properties, so the page reads current in Logseq.

The tools (`knowledge_search`, `knowledge_write`, `knowledge_read`
and `knowledge_status`) are offered to workspace episodes only; every
other session keeps the harness's memory tools.  Memories are the
small behavioral notes -- how the user wants work done -- and the
workspace's own prompt says so.

The module is deliberately not an index: a search reads the graph and
ranks the blocks it finds (harness-logseq/search).  The graph can be
large, so a search reads the newest pages and journals first and
stops at `harness-logseq-search-pages` and `...-journal-pages`.  A
later stage can put an index in front of the same answers without
changing this contract.

## Provides

### Methods

- `knowledge/notes` (workspace &optional opts) — Return the newest blocks of WORKSPACE's knowledge, newest first.
- `knowledge/page` (workspace page &optional opts) — Return PAGE of WORKSPACE's graph with its blocks.
- `knowledge/pages` (workspace &optional filter) — Return the pages of WORKSPACE's graph it made for its threads.
- `knowledge/recall` (workspace thread text &optional opts) — Return what a brief recalls for TEXT in WORKSPACE's THREAD.
- `knowledge/remember` (session-id text &optional thread) — Write TEXT as knowledge for SESSION-ID's workspace and THREAD.
- `knowledge/search` (workspace query &optional opts) — Return the blocks of WORKSPACE's knowledge graph that match QUERY.
- `knowledge/status` (&optional workspace) — Return what WORKSPACE's knowledge graph holds, or nil for no workspace.
- `knowledge/thread-page` (workspace thread) — Return THREAD's page name in WORKSPACE's graph, creating it.
- `knowledge/thread-touch` (workspace thread &optional status) — Bring THREAD's page in WORKSPACE up to date: STATUS and last-touched.
- `knowledge/write` (workspace thread role text &optional opts) — Write TEXT as durable knowledge of WORKSPACE's THREAD, as ROLE.

### Tools

- `knowledge_read` — Read one page of the workspace's Logseq graph by name, such as a thread's page or Projects/harness. Returns the page's blocks, newest last.
- `knowledge_search` — Search the workspace's Logseq knowledge graph: decisions, facts, projects, people and the notes of every thread. Use it for anything the brief did not give you, for what another thread learned, or for a preference the user wrote down. Set all to search the user's whole graph, not only this workspace. Never invent knowledge you did not retrieve.
- `knowledge_status` — Say what the workspace's Logseq graph holds: blocks, pages, the graph root and when it last changed.
- `knowledge_write` — Write durable knowledge to the workspace's Logseq graph: a decision, a fact, a commitment, an open loop or a next action. The block goes on the current thread's page unless page names another one (Projects/harness, Preferences, People/Ada). Write one concise statement, not a transcript dump; the user's own edits in Logseq outrank what you write.

### Events

- `workspace/knowledge-changed` — (WORKSPACE OP) when a block was written to the workspace's graph.

### Options

- `harness-workspace-knowledge-capture-chars` — Most characters of one message the journal capture keeps.
- `harness-workspace-knowledge-recall-limit` — Blocks a brief recalls from the graph.
- `harness-workspace-knowledge-status-seconds` — Seconds a workspace's knowledge status is kept before it is read again.
- `harness-workspace-knowledge-thread-blocks` — Blocks a brief quotes from the thread's own page.
